A set of end-to-end **Pintelon–Schoukens** campaigns, ordered from the simplest single
resonance through a coupled 2×2 MIMO suspension, a DARM calibration loop, and a joint
6-DoF modal identification through live damping loops. The single-plant examples run the
*same* full diagnostic set — excitation design, measurement time series,
magnitude/phase/coherence Bode, residuals, Cramér–Rao parameter recovery, drive-safety
margins, convergence, and the pass-by-pass overlay — so you can read any one and know your
way around all of them; the closed-loop MIMO and calibration pages reuse the same
leakage-free FRF and Cramér–Rao machinery on their own plants.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## A note on the plant models
These are **simplified, physically-motivated** teaching plants — lumped resonances and, in
the [MIMO example](06-two-by-two-coupled.qmd), a coupled longitudinal/pitch normal-mode
expansion — **not** validated full Advanced-LIGO suspension state-space models. Where used,
mode frequencies are *representative* aLIGO quad rigid-body values (longitudinal ≈ 0.43,
1.00, 2.01, 3.42 Hz; pitch ≈ 0.56, 1.31, 2.81 Hz; Aston *et al.* 2012,
[DCC P1200056](https://dcc.ligo.org/LIGO-P1200056); Sauter *et al.* 2024,
[arXiv:2306.13755](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.13755)). The method, not the plant, is the
point — it applies unchanged to a measured or higher-fidelity model.
:::
